definitions.gloss: peerage; title of nobility; rank of nobility
definitions.explanation: A hereditary or granted rank within a system of nobility. In Japan, the peerage system (華族制度) existed from 1869 to 1947.

examples.japanese: {爵位|しゃくい}を{授|さず}ける。
examples.english: To confer a title of nobility.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{功績|こうせき}により{爵位|しゃくい}を{与|あた}えられた。
examples.english: He was granted a peerage for his achievements.

examples.japanese: {戦後|せんご}の{改革|かいかく}で{日本|にほん}の{爵位|しゃくい}{制度|せいど}は{廃止|はいし}された。
examples.english: Japan's peerage system was abolished in the postwar reforms.

notes: Japan had a five-rank peerage system modeled on European nobility: {公爵|こうしゃく} (duke/prince), {侯爵|こうしゃく} (marquis), {伯爵|はくしゃく} (count/earl), {子爵|ししゃく} (viscount), and {男爵|だんしゃく} (baron). This system was abolished with the 1947 constitution. The word now appears mainly in historical contexts and translations of Western literature. Common collocations: {爵位|しゃくい}を{授|さず}ける (confer a peerage), {爵位|しゃくい}を{剥奪|はくだつ}する (strip of a peerage).
